title: Kinematics
standard_text: Distance, displacement, speed, velocity and acceleration; position–time and velocity–time graphs; the equations of uniformly accelerated motion; free fall; and motion in two dimensions with vectors. (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 11 and 12: Science (2008), Physics, Grade 11, University Preparation (SPH3U), Strand B: Kinematics)
meta_desc: Free Grade 11 Physics (SPH3U) worksheets on kinematics: displacement and velocity, acceleration, motion graphs, the kinematics equations, free fall and two-dimensional vectors. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Velocity is the slope of a position–time graph; acceleration is the slope of a velocity–time graph.
body_html:
How to think about it

Displacement and velocity are vectors: they have a direction. Average velocity = displacement ÷ time; acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time. On a velocity–time graph, the slope is the acceleration and the area under the line is the displacement.

For constant acceleration use v₂ = v₁ + aΔt, Δd = v₁Δt + ½aΔt², v₂² = v₁² + 2aΔd and Δd = ½(v₁ + v₂)Δt. Choose a positive direction first. In free fall the acceleration is 9.8 m/s² downwards.

Example

A car speeds up from 10 m/s to 25 m/s in 5.0 s. Acceleration?

a = (25 − 10) ÷ 5.0

Answer: 3.0 m/s²

Example

A stone is dropped from rest. Speed after 2.0 s?

v = 9.8 × 2.0

Answer: 19.6 m/s

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up distance and displacement after a round trip.
  • Forgetting signs: an object thrown up has a negative acceleration if up is positive.
  • Reading the height of a v–t graph as the displacement instead of the area.

faq.q: What is the velocity at the top of a ball's flight?
faq.a: Zero vertically; the acceleration is still 9.8 m/s² downwards.

faq.q: How do you add two perpendicular vectors?
faq.a: Draw them tip to tail and use the Pythagorean theorem for the size and tan θ for the direction.
